verdict.line: You lose if you ever let him pull you into a stand-still trade or get caught by his level 6+ Realm of Death; you win if you poke from outside 700 range and never give him three free hits to pop Darkness Rise.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser has nothing that reaches past 700 range — Q (Obliterate, 675 range) and E (Death's Grasp, 700 range) both require him to close the gap, while your Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) does not. The 50.3% win rate over 187 games reflects that even poke war, offset by his real edge: once he lands the pull or gets three hits to trigger Darkness Rise, his duel and R (Realm of Death) threat outscales anything you can trade back in melee range.

theirWindow.when: E up and you're inside 700 range
theirWindow.what: He can pull you point-blank and follow with Obliterate plus autos to trigger Darkness Rise. Back off to 1100 range or past 700 the moment you see his E come off cooldown.

yourWindow.when: His E (Death's Grasp) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Walk up to the 700-1100 band and throw Q (Boomerang Throw) freely — he has no other way to close the distance, so this is your free poke window.

start.why: Run by 45.5% of players at 66.7% pick rate — the sustain and early AD lets you trade Q pokes and tank a stray Obliterate without losing lane state.

boots.why: 68.8% pick rate at 55.3% win rate — Mordekaiser's entire kit is magic damage, and the tenacity matters if his E pull connects.

core.why: Highest-winrate path (60.9% over 23 games) — the move speed proc keeps you at Q range and off his Obliterate/Death's Grasp distance.

runes.keystoneWhy: Highest-winrate page (50.7% over this sample at 31.8% pick) — the move speed and sustain on hit directly supports the poke-and-retreat pattern this matchup demands. Master-tier Gnar players instead run Lethal Tempo (1,803 games) — better suited if you plan to stand and trade autos rather than kite, which is riskier into his pull.

summoners.why: 61.9% pick rate — this is a defensive-shaped lane where you're often shoved off wave, and Teleport lets you reset without losing tempo. Flash+Ignite (56.1% win rate, 17.4% pick) is the better pick if you're ahead and want to punish a bad Death's Grasp with a kill.

playing.title: Never melee-trade him
playing.detail: He has no gap-closer besides Death's Grasp (E, 700 range). If you're outside that range and he hasn't pulled you, he physically cannot force a fight — stay on Q cooldown at 1100 range instead of walking up.

playing.title: Dodge his E with your E
playing.detail: Use Hop (E) reactively to reposition out of Death's Grasp's area before it resolves — this is the single highest-value defensive play in the matchup.

playing.title: Count his Darkness Rise stacks
playing.detail: After 3 landed attacks or spells on you he gets a damage aura and move speed. Break off the trade before he reaches that third hit, don't let him farm it for free.

playing.title: Respect level 6-10 hard
playing.detail: Realm of Death (R, 650 range) is his kill button and the data's solo-kill edge comes from exactly this window. Don't extend trades or overstay a wave once he's level 6.

playing.title: Manage your Rage bar on purpose
playing.detail: Transforming into Mega Gnar mid-trade trades your 1100-range Q for a point-blank boulder throw — don't let Rage fill passively into his pull range, time the transform for when you're initiating, not defending.

playing.title: Punish his shield consumption
playing.detail: Indestructible (W) stores damage to heal later — if he consumes it to top off, that's your window to re-engage with Q before the shield rebuilds.

playing.title: Group around level 6 if behind
playing.detail: Since the data shows he wins the 1v1 duel more often, look to draw a gank rather than force a solo kill once his ultimate is up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win rates above are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning (range bands, Darkness Rise timing, Rage bar management) is this brief's own tactical read, not OP.GG's.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid fighting him head on, while using [E] to dodge his (E). Kite him while keeping your distance to gain the upper hand.
